findings.evidence: Ideal.lean:148-158 (`open Classical in` immediately above `@[simp] theorem indVirtualCharactersAddHom_of`). `DirectSum.of` and `DirectSum.toAddMonoid` sit inside `section DecidableEq` / `variable [DecidableEq ι]` in mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean:118ff, and `toAddMonoid_of` (line 226) carries that binder rather than a classical instance.
findings.fix: Drop `open Classical in` and state the theorem with `[DecidableEq {S : Subgroup G // P S}]` as an instance binder, as Mathlib's `DirectSum.toAddMonoid_of` does; discharge the mismatch against the classical instance baked into the definition with `Subsingleton.elim`/`congr`.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharactersAddHom_of` is the only computation rule for `indVirtualCharactersAddHom` (whose body is not exposed), but `open Classical in` elaborates the `DecidableEq {S : Subgroup G // P S}` argument of `DirectSum.of` to a fixed `Classical.propDecidable` term inside the statement instead of leaving it an instance binder. A consumer who writes a lemma with `[DecidableEq {S : Subgroup G // P S}]` in context — the natural way to build `DirectSum.of` terms — gets a `simp`/`rw` that does not fire, since the two instances are not defeq, and has no other handle on the map.

findings.evidence: Named-argument boilerplate at Ideal.lean:146, 153, 164, 179 and Artin.lean:359, 368-370, 380, 395; contrast `variable (k G) in` before `def indVirtualCharacters` at Ideal.lean:77-83.
findings.fix: Wrap the definitions in `variable (k G) in` so they read `indVirtualCharactersAddHom k G P` and `cyclicInductionRatLinearMap k G`, matching `indVirtualCharacters k G P`, and drop the named arguments at the use sites.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharactersAddHom` (and `indVirtualCharactersComponent`, and `cyclicInductionRatLinearMap` in Artin.lean) leave `k` and `G` implicit, but `k` occurs only in the (co)domain, so it is not inferable from the explicit arguments. Every single use site in the PR is forced to write `(k := k) (G := G)`, and the sibling definition `indVirtualCharacters k G P` takes them explicitly, so the two spellings of the same object diverge.

findings.evidence: Artin.lean:97-112. mathlib/Mathlib/Order/Interval/Finset/Defs.lean:567-572: "This is not an instance as it would not be defeq to better instances"; mathlib/MathlibTest/InstanceDiamonds.lean:215-218 records the diamond against `Subtype.instLocallyFiniteOrder` (a global instance at Defs.lean:928).
findings.fix: Make all three `local instance` (or `letI`/`haveI` inside the three private declarations that need them) — the repo already uses `attribute [local instance]` for exactly this, e.g. TauCeti/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent/Localization.lean:42.
findings.issue: `cyclicSubgroupFintype`, `cyclicSubgroupLocallyFiniteOrder` and `cyclicSubgroupLocallyFiniteOrderTop` are registered as global `instance`s on `{C : Subgroup G // IsCyclic C}` — via a reducible `abbrev`, so the keys are the bare subtype, which is exactly the index type of the public `cyclicInductionRatLinearMap` and of `indVirtualCharactersAddHom (fun C ↦ IsCyclic C)`. Mathlib deliberately refuses to make `Fintype.toLocallyFiniteOrder` an instance because it is not defeq to `Subtype.instLocallyFiniteOrder`, and `Fintype.ofFinite` is never a global instance because it is noncomputable and competes with `Subtype.fintype`; both hazards are reintroduced here on a type that appears in this file's public signatures.

summary: The canonical target and the deletion of the subsumed restatements are right, but the bundled direct-sum map is awkward to use: its sole computation rule freezes a classical `DecidableEq` in the statement, and `k`/`G` are implicit on both new definitions so every use site needs named arguments. The three helper instances on the cyclic-subgroup subtype are also registered globally rather than locally.
